method: Independent read-only review of all 197 files assigned by .work/round5/interface.json, including every core and gateway module, all assigned tests, all web components/hooks/helpers/styles/configuration and web/VERIFICATION.md; output sections truncated by the tool were read again. Also read AGENTS.md, package.json, scripts/run-tests.mjs, scripts/snapshot.mjs and vitest.config.ts as current supporting context. Traced input validation and authentication/session/Origin/Host/CSRF boundaries, browser/worker ownership and reconnect cleanup, mutation receipt reservation/replay/redaction/unknown outcomes, budgets and scheduler admission, UI draft and history state, explicit resume and action admission, approvals, account/provider/remote/extension flows, terminal/process/realtime lifecycles, model/media/context selection, workspace version checks/recovery/Git, organization and automation workflows. Cross-checked source against current tests and then ran 12 explicitly selected repository test files (130 passing cases) using isolated temporary paths under .work/round5. React duplicate-key warnings observed in this run led to a new focused two-case jsdom reproduction under ignored .work/round5 using the actual Composer and useDraft modules; both regression assertions failed and established the finding below. No old repository, Git history, prior audit artifact, external service, personal credentials or full test suite was inspected/run. The assigned web/VERIFICATION.md itself contains historical implementation/audit summaries; those required current-document contents were read, but their conclusions and referenced evidence were not used as audit proof. No source/test/documentation changes were made. Only ignored reproduction material and this requested audit artifact were written. Source snapshot was recomputed after testing and remained unchanged. Complete means assigned source review completed; this round is not clean because it contains one verified actionable defect.

findings.impact: EnvironmentPicker and InputContextPicker are sibling elements with the same key={contextKey}. When navigation changes contextKey, React leaves the old EnvironmentPicker mounted in the DOM. Repeated navigation accumulates duplicate environment controls with stale callbacks. Clicking a retained control can erase the previous conversation draft: its captured useDraft update closure sees a different current key, uses emptyDraft(oldKey), and persists that empty draft. It also leaves the currently displayed draft empty until reloaded. This affects normal thread/new-draft navigation because App changes attachmentContext on navigation and passes it to the same mounted Composer. Give the sibling controls distinct keys and cover navigation plus stale callback ownership with a regression test.

source: web/components/Composer.tsx:50 uses the identical key for the two sibling controls
web/App.tsx:134 and :143 change attachmentContext on browser/direct navigation; :193 passes it as Composer contextKey without remounting Composer
web/hooks/useDraft.ts:12-15 initializes emptyDraft(key) when an old update closure runs while current.current.key belongs to another draft
observed: Rendering actual Composer with contexts a, b and c produced environment-picker counts [1,2,3], where [1,1,1] was expected; clicking the oldest retained control invoked options {model:"model-a"}.

With actual useDraft and persisted texts a="unsent A" and b="unsent B", render a, navigate to b, then click the old environment control: readDraft("a").text became "", readDraft("b").text stayed "unsent B", and the displayed textarea became "".
evidence.result: 2 focused regression assertions failed as expected against the frozen source; both failures directly reproduce the defect.
